definition-dropped.flag: character | in a coded character set (newer: undefined); character | in a screen item (newer: undefined); character | in cobol character repertoire (newer: undefined); character | in computer storage (newer: undefined); coded character set (newer: undefined); national character (newer: undefined)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 defines 'character' in four senses (in a coded character set, in a screen item, in the COBOL character repertoire, in computer storage) and 'coded character set' as "A set of unambiguous rules that establishes a character set" (taken from ISO/IEC 10646-1); 2023 drops these entries and takes the terms from its normative reference ISO/IEC 10646 (§2023:2), in the same sense. GR5's 'character classification' is a locale's LC_CTYPE classification, not one of the dropped entries; the ten cases the reader listed are unchanged. 'national character' (§2002:4: "A character in a national character set") is the same notion 2023 uses with its kept 'national character set' entry (§2023:3.125); this compiler's national set is UTF-16 in both editions.

pending-clause.answer: Not dependent: GR5 takes the classification from the current locale (§2002:12.2.5.3 GR5), and 8.1.1's differing text (2023's single coded values for figurative constants and editing characters, and the currency prohibition) does not bear on classification; the evidence is runs at --std 2002.
